analysis.title: Positioning Mondays - Week 44
key_insights: De-grossing accelerated for a 3rd straight week on the GS prime book, driven by short covers outpacing long sales at 1.8 to 1.
The GS US desk saw $4.2bn of net Tech selling on Friday only by institutional clients.
Asset Managers finished the week as net sellers, more than reversing earlier week demand in Tech.
October performance was weak: Global Fundamental L/S managers -3.5%, Global Systematic L/S managers -3.6%, Multi-Strats -0.9%.
Gross levels remain near the top of the historical range, at the 94th 5-year percentile for Fundamental L/S in the GS PB book.

The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had its largest monthly drop since November 2021 in October but has not reached levels that signal a contrarian buying opportunity. AAII, CNN Fear & Greed and GS SI show the same.

Global equities were net bought for the first time in a month (+0.3 SDs 1-year). Single stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week, driven by long sales, while macro products were net bought for a 2nd straight week.
Industrials, Staples and Energy were the most net sold global sectors by dollars. TMT (Comm Svcs + Info Tech) and Real Estate were the most net bought.
Europe saw risk-off flows for a 3rd consecutive week, with long sales outpacing short covers 1.8:1. North America remains underweight at -15% in the GS book.

CTAs sold $1bn of Global Equities over the week and are expected to be marginal sellers over the next month. They would need to sell about $11.5bn over one month in a flat market, concentrated in US indices.

Corporate buyback desk activity ran 0.6x vs 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.7x vs 2024 YTD ADTV, with the mix shifting to 22% discretionary open market flow vs 78% 10b5-1. November is historically the desk's second most active month.

Global equity funds saw net inflows of +$56bn in the week ending October 28, with technology funds again taking the largest net inflows and utilities the largest net outflows. Brazil funds saw net outflows after the second-round election results.
Events ahead this week: Apple earnings, ISM, US midterms, the Treasury quarterly refunding announcement (QRA) and NFP.

vol_and_positioning: Overall book gross leverage +1.8 pts to 314.1% (86th percentile 1-year). Net leverage +1.8 pts to 73.6% (10th percentile 1-year). L/S ratio +0.9% to 1.612 (8th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage +0.4 pts to 212.1% (69th percentile 1-year). Net leverage +2.4 pts to 49.4% (3rd percentile 1-year).
Beta adjusted Fundamental L/S gross leverage +3.1 pts to 229.7% (39th percentile 1-year). Beta adjusted net leverage +4.4 pts to 64.8% (3rd percentile 1-year).
Europe is overweight vs MSCI World in the GS book by 3.47%, up 0.24 ppts WoW. North America is underweight at -15%, reduced by 1.06 ppts.

CTAs hold about $49bn of Global Equities (48th percentile). Models predict marginal buying over a one-week horizon in a flat market. S&P E-mini levels to watch: 7712 (ST threshold), 7544 (MT), 7081 (LT).
Retail flows were volatile, but the daily Buy-Sell skew was positive every day of the week.
AAII survey for the week ending October 28: Bulls 37.8%, Bears 41.4%, Neutral 20.7%, vs historical averages of 37.5% / 31% / 31.5%.
GS Sentiment Indicator edged up to +0.2 from -0.2 a week ago. CNN Fear & Greed is 27/100 vs 29/100 last week.
Asset Managers were small net buyers of S&P futures in the week ending October 27 per CFTC data.
geopolitical: Brazil funds saw net outflows following the second-round election results.
US midterms are listed among the events ahead this week.
